# University of Melbourne: Overview
The University of Melbourne, founded in 1853, is a leading Australian research university based primarily at the Parkville campus in Melbourne, with several metropolitan and regional campuses including Burnley, Southbank, Werribee, Creswick, Dookie, and Shepparton. It is governed by a 13-member University Council under the University of Melbourne Act 2009, with operational and academic oversight from the Academic Board. As of 2025, Emma Johnston serves as Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to hold the position. The university comprises nine faculties covering architecture, arts, business, education, engineering, fine arts, law, medicine, and science. Distinctively, the "Melbourne Model" offers broad three-year undergraduate degrees followed by professional graduate study.
Melbourne is consistently ranked as the top university in Australia and among the world's best in major international rankings (QS, THE, ARWU, US News), and has a robust research profile, with the largest cohort of research students nationally and extensive external research funding. The university is recognized for its academic collections—with twelve libraries and several museums, including the Grainger Museum, Ian Potter Museum of Art, and Science Gallery Melbourne—housing millions of items and supporting over 100 research centers. Notable alumni include several Australian Prime Ministers, Nobel laureates such as Elizabeth Blackburn, and prominent figures in arts and sciences. The university's student body is highly international, clubs and societies are vibrant, and student outcomes for employment and satisfaction remain among the highest in the country.
